engineering.verdict: Real, tested, production software - but sitting just BELOW its own Tier P target band, and the reason is specific.

evidence_run_today.lint: npm run lint -> exit 0, no problems
evidence_run_today.typecheck: npm run typecheck -> exit 0, no errors (strict)
evidence_run_today.tests: npm test -> 1836 passed across 214 files, exit 0
evidence_run_today.build: npm run build -> exit 0, webpack production build

met: Real business-logic tests, not a smoke suite - 214 files covering suppression, send governance, per-mailbox caps, warm-up ramp, unsubscribe rails, bounce policy and reply matching, with genuine fail-closed assertions
Merge-blocking CI gate, branch protection on main
Automated deploy via Entra OIDC with a post-deploy health check, verified by commit rather than liveness
Secrets gitignored; .env.example is the committed template
Error monitoring wired (Sentry server + edge configs)
not_met: NO e2e coverage of critical journey J5 - enrol, launch, send, reply, opt-out. The Playwright suite covers authentication, staff role boundaries and outbound-email detail; it does not cover the journey that actually reaches a third party's inbox. This is the single biggest reason this is not a 9.
Coverage thresholds are NOT verified as enforced. A test:coverage script exists; whether CI fails below a threshold was not checked today, so it is not claimed.
Sentry is configured but I did not verify it is RECEIVING events in production. Wired is not the same as live.
engineering.why_not_higher: The standard is explicit that a 9 requires strict typecheck, lint, real tests AND enforced coverage, e2e on critical journeys, live error monitoring, gitignored secrets, a merge-blocking CI gate, and automated deploy plus health check - ALL present and passing. Three of those are unproven or absent. Rounding to 8.5 to land inside the tier band would be exactly the false-9 the protocol exists to prevent.
engineering.why_not_lower: 1836 genuine tests with fail-closed assertions on the send path is not a scaffold. Every gate that was run, passed.

customer_ready.status: GRADED 2026-08-09 by walking production live as a signed-in operator
customer_ready.cap_applied: Core customer journey broken/not functional -> cap 4.0. A judgement call, stated openly in the report: the send journey is not mechanically broken (mail leaves, 1,209 sends carry provider proof) but production still mints unsubscribe links on the OpensDoors app domain while From: is the customer's own domain - the exact phishing pattern that caused the quarantine. A journey that completes while defeating its own purpose is not a working journey from the customer's side. If the cap is rejected, the honest uncapped number is 6.0; either way it is below 8 and the required actions are identical.
customer_ready.decisive_evidence: Deployed commit b36e66e contains send-introduction.ts:529 `resolveClientLinkBaseUrl(client) ?? resolvePublicBaseUrl()`. No client has a verified aligned link domain, so it falls through to AUTH_URL = https://opensdoors.bidlow.co.uk. The fix (commit a8d777c) exists on the UNMERGED branch feat/zero-dns-send-profile. The other half of the root cause IS fixed and live: OPEN_TRACKING_PIXEL=off, verified against Azure config today.
customer_ready.why_not_higher: Beyond the link defect: the Train Hugger workspace shows 'LATEST ACTIVITY - No sends yet' while the reporting page shows 743 sends for that same client, so operators are shown two different truths; bounces read 0 (0%) across 1,209 sends because there are no delivery webhooks, making a stated non-negotiable unenforceable; 204 of ~1,470 contacts show 'send proof missing'; /operations 404s and /clients/{id}/activity silently redirects.
customer_ready.why_not_lower: This is not a scaffold. Dev-ism hygiene is genuinely strong (9/10) - friendly labels, no raw enums or cuids, 'Workspace ID' not 'Slug'. UX is good (8/10): a numbered setup workflow, a real launch-readiness panel, and a danger zone that states precisely what deletion does and does not touch and requires typing the workspace name. Auth held and no cross-customer leakage was seen.
findings_so_far: Reporting dashboard renders real live data cleanly and states its own methodology ('live counts, no rollup tables'; sends counted only with provider proof). Reads as trustworthy.
PWA install prompt is present and correct, satisfying the standing BidlowAI PWA rule.
204 of ~1,470 contacts show 'send proof missing' (~14%), against 1,209 sends with proof. Unexplained, and material to whether an operator can trust the numbers.

Delivered shows 'Not tracked - no provider delivery webhooks yet'; Bounces read 0 (0%) and Opens 0 across 1,209 sends. The domain brief makes bounce rate below 2% a non-negotiable. A 0% reading with no delivery webhooks most likely means bounces are not being DETECTED. A threshold that cannot be measured cannot be enforced - this is the most important open question on the product.
/operations returned 404 on production. Not diagnosed; may be a moved route rather than a defect.
Known, pre-existing: the Google OAuth app remains in Testing mode, so Google-connected mailboxes need reconnecting roughly weekly. Recurring, customer-visible friction.
customer_ready.how_to_complete: Run the customer-ready-audit skill as its own focused session, walk the product as a customer against the full rubric, and save a dated CUSTOMER-READY-REPORT.md. The placeholder file in the repo root already records the known caps.

sell_gate.result: NOT SATISFIED. Fix the lower grade first: Customer-Ready. The single highest-impact action is to review, merge and deploy feat/zero-dns-send-profile, which removes the app-domain unsubscribe links from production. Push and deploy remain blocked.
